body:
## Summary
Add a `qq` shell command that sends a single, context-free question to the configured AI backend (`opencode` / `claude` / `agy`) and prints the answer. `qq` with no args opens a `qq> ` prompt; `qq some question` passes the typed text verbatim (no shell escaping needed). Backend and model settings are shared with `commit` under renamed `DOTFILES_AI_*` env vars, and the shared helpers move into a new `lib/ai.sh`.

## Motivation / Context
Raw idea (user's words):

> add a 'qq' command that uses the same model env vars and settings as 'commit'. When you run 'qq' with no parameters, it opens an input prompt that lets you ask a single question that gets passed to the configured AI agent harness as a one-off command and it returns the response. Open to an additional feature where you run 'qq this is a question' and it passes all parameters as a prompt. However, we'd need to consider whether it's too brittle with all of the escaping needed. or it could be "qq 'this is a question'" as a backup. The 'c' alias has worked fairly well in passing additional args to the commit message with minimal friction (even with some escaped character quirks), so I'm not too concerned. catching special characters that need to be escaped and throwing an error could be a good middle ground

Existing overlap: `commit` in `lib/git.sh` already resolves backend/model/timeout via `_dotfiles_commit_backend` (`DOTFILES_COMMIT_BACKEND`, default `opencode`; also `claude`, `agy`), `_dotfiles_commit_model` (`DOTFILES_COMMIT_MODEL`, per-backend defaults), `_dotfiles_commit_timeout` (`DOTFILES_COMMIT_TIMEOUT`, default 15s), and shows a spinner via `_dotfiles_spinner_wait`. `c` joins args with `"$*"`.

## Requirements
- **Shared AI settings, renamed:** the backend/model env vars shared by `commit` and `qq` are renamed from `DOTFILES_COMMIT_*` to `DOTFILES_AI_*`:
  - `DOTFILES_COMMIT_BACKEND` → `DOTFILES_AI_BACKEND` (same values: `opencode` default, `claude`, `agy`)
  - `DOTFILES_COMMIT_MODEL` → `DOTFILES_AI_MODEL` (same per-backend defaults when unset)
  - `qq` and `commit` resolve backend and model through the same shared helpers, so one setting drives both.
- **Deprecated-name fallback:** if `DOTFILES_AI_BACKEND` / `DOTFILES_AI_MODEL` is unset but the old `DOTFILES_COMMIT_BACKEND` / `DOTFILES_COMMIT_MODEL` is set, the old value is used and a one-line deprecation warning naming the new variable is printed to stderr (never stdout, so captured output stays clean). When the new name is set, it wins and no warning is printed.
- **Per-command timeouts:** `qq` gets its own timeout var `DOTFILES_QQ_TIMEOUT` with a longer default than commit's (commit's 15s is tuned for a one-line message). `commit` keeps its own timeout (`DOTFILES_COMMIT_TIMEOUT`, default 15s) — timeouts are per-command, not shared.
- **Structure — new `lib/ai.sh`:** the shared helpers move out of `lib/git.sh` into a new `lib/ai.sh` and are renamed to `_dotfiles_ai_*` (backend resolution, model resolution, the spinner `_dotfiles_spinner_wait` → `_dotfiles_ai_spinner_wait`, and a shared timeout parser — see Refactor scope). `qq` is defined in `lib/ai.sh`. `commit` in `lib/git.sh` calls the shared `_dotfiles_ai_*` helpers.
- **`commit` subcommands:** `commit backend X` now exports `DOTFILES_AI_BACKEND` (so it switches `qq`'s backend too). `commit status` also shows the `qq` timeout alongside the existing backend/model/timeout/available lines.
- **No `qq` subcommands:** `qq` has no subcommands, so any input — e.g. `qq status of my PR` — is always treated as a question.
- **Prompt wrapper:** `qq` prepends a short fixed instruction to the question before sending it to the backend, e.g. "Answer concisely for display in a terminal. Prefer short answers; use code blocks for commands." followed by the question. The wrapper is fixed (no env override).
- **Context-free:** `qq` is pure Q&A with no repo/file access. The backend is invoked outside the user's cwd (e.g. from a temporary empty directory) and, where the backend CLI supports it, with tools disabled — so answers don't depend on or read local files. Exact per-backend flags are an implementation detail to verify against each CLI's current docs. The user's shell cwd is unchanged after `qq` returns.
- **Refactor scope:**
  - `lib/ai.sh` (new): `_dotfiles_ai_backend` / `_dotfiles_ai_model` (reading `DOTFILES_AI_*` with the deprecated-name fallback + warning), the spinner (`_dotfiles_spinner_wait` → `_dotfiles_ai_spinner_wait`), a small timeout parser parameterized by variable name and default (so commit's 15s and qq's 60s share it), and `_dotfiles_qq` + the `qq` alias.
  - `lib/git.sh`: `commit` / `_dotfiles_commit_generate_message` call the `_dotfiles_ai_*` helpers; commit-specific pieces (prompt, sanitize, `DOTFILES_COMMIT_TIMEOUT`) stay in `git.sh`.
  - `lib/index.sh`: no change (it already sources every `lib/*.sh`).
- **Docs:** update `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` — renamed vars + deprecation fallback, `DOTFILES_QQ_TIMEOUT`, and a short `qq` usage note (args form vs. bare `qq`, the `!word` and leading-space limits, piping only with bare `qq`).
- **`DOTFILES_QQ_TIMEOUT` default: 60s.** Parsing mirrors commit's timeout parser: empty or non-numeric falls back to the default (60); `0` means no timeout (wait until the backend finishes; Ctrl-C still cancels).
- **Runtime flow:** (1) obtain the question — interactive shells use the raw history line, non-interactive calls use `"$*"`; in either case, if the result is empty, fall through to the `qq> ` prompt; (2) resolve backend + model via `_dotfiles_ai_*`; (3) launch the backend in the background from a temporary empty directory with wrapper + question; (4) show the existing spinner on **stderr** (e.g. `Asking Opencode...`); (5) print the answer to **stdout** as-is — multi-line, code blocks intact; unlike `commit` it is not truncated to one line, only leading/trailing blank lines are trimmed; (6) clean up the temp dir and output file.
- **Stdout is answer-only:** everything except the answer (spinner, warnings, errors) goes to stderr. Note: with the raw-history args form, a trailing `| cmd` on the `qq` line is part of the question, so piping the answer works with bare `qq` or non-interactive calls.
- **No manual fallback:** unlike `commit` (which falls back to `c`), every `qq` error prints one line to stderr and exits non-zero:

  | Case | Message (stderr) | Exit |
  |---|---|---|
  | Empty input / Ctrl-D / Ctrl-C at `qq>` | (none) | 1 (130 on Ctrl-C) |
  | Leading-space guard trips | `qq: question not in history (leading space?); run bare qq instead` | 1 |
  | Backend CLI not installed | `qq: <backend> not found` | 1 |
  | Ctrl-C while waiting | `qq canceled` | 130 |
  | Timeout | `qq: <backend> timed out after <N>s` | 124 |
  | Backend fails / empty output | `qq: <backend> returned no answer` | 1 |
- **No-arg input prompt:** bare `qq` shows a `qq> ` prompt and reads one line with `read -e -r` (readline editing; the text is not parsed by the shell, so no escaping is needed). Enter submits. Empty input, Ctrl-D, or Ctrl-C exits without calling the AI backend.
- **Args-as-prompt via raw history line:** `qq this is a question` captures the question exactly as typed, not via `"$*"`:
  - Define `alias qq='_dotfiles_qq #'`. The trailing `#` makes bash treat the rest of the line as a comment, so it is not parsed, expanded, globbed, or redirected.
  - `_dotfiles_qq` reads the current command line from `history 1` (with `HISTTIMEFORMAT` neutralized), strips the history number and everything up to and including the `qq` invocation, and uses the remainder verbatim as the question.
  - Result: `? * $VAR > < ; & | ' "` all pass through literally (verified in a throwaway spike: `what's up`, `a > b means what`, `$HOME`, `*`, `?`, `;`, and double quotes all arrived verbatim, and no redirect file was created).
  - If the remainder is empty (bare `qq`), fall through to the `qq> ` input prompt.
- **Leading-space guard:** the user's `bash_profile` sets `HISTCONTROL=ignorespace`, so a command typed with a leading space is not saved to history and `history 1` returns the *previous* entry (the spike showed this silently re-sending an older question). `_dotfiles_qq` must detect that the current command was not recorded to history and exit non-zero with an error telling the user to run bare `qq` instead — it must never send a stale history entry.
- **Non-interactive fallback:** in scripts / non-interactive shells (aliases and history inactive), `_dotfiles_qq` is called directly with real args and uses `"$*"` as the question.
- **Known limitation — `!word`:** bash history expansion runs before the comment is recognized, so `qq is !important bad` fails with bash's own `event not found` error and nothing is sent. This is visible (not silent) and is documented rather than worked around.
- **Known limitation — line continuation:** a trailing `\` continuation is not supported in the args form (only the first physical line is recorded); use bare `qq` for such input.

## Non-goals
- Multi-turn chat / follow-up questions
- Repo-aware answers (file reads, tools)
- Streaming output
- Markdown rendering
- Reading the question from piped stdin
- `qq` subcommands
- An env override for the wrapper prompt
- Working around `!word` bash history expansion

## Testing
Bats tests, written TDD-first, following the existing pattern (source libs in `bash -c`, stub `claude` / `opencode` / `agy` as shell functions):

- **Existing tests updated** for the renamed vars/helpers: `tests/commit_backend.bats`, `tests/commit_command.bats`, `tests/commit_generate_message.bats`, `tests/spinner_wait.bats`.
- **Deprecation fallback:** only the old name set → its value is used and a warning is printed on stderr; new name set → it wins and no warning; the warning never appears on stdout.
- **New `tests/qq_command.bats`:**
  - Non-interactive args form uses `"$*"`.
  - Raw-history path, exercised under `bash -i` with an rcfile (as in the spike): `?`, `*`, `$HOME`, `>`, `;`, `'` arrive verbatim, and no redirect file is created.
  - Leading-space guard errors and does **not** send the previous history entry.
  - Bare `qq` with empty input exits 1 without calling the backend.
  - The terminal wrapper text is included in the prompt sent to the backend.
  - The backend runs in a directory other than `$PWD`, and the caller's cwd is unchanged afterwards.
  - Multi-line answers are preserved; leading/trailing blank lines are trimmed.
  - Error table rows: backend not found → exit 1; timeout (short `DOTFILES_QQ_TIMEOUT`) → exit 124; empty answer → exit 1.
  - stdout contains only the answer.
- **`tests/lib_modules.bats`:** add a `type qq` check for `ai.sh`.
- **Quality gates:** `bashcheck` on changed lib files, then `just test-unit` and `just test`.

## Open decisions
- None. (Exact per-backend flags for disabling tools are an implementation detail to verify against each CLI's current docs.)

<details>
<summary>Brainstorm log</summary>

- [x] Q: Should `qq` share commit's settings exactly (same env vars, same backend/model) or get its own overridable vars that fall back to commit's? A: Share backend + model, but `qq` gets its own timeout. Rename all shared env vars to `DOTFILES_AI_*`.
- [x] Q: Should the old `DOTFILES_COMMIT_BACKEND` / `DOTFILES_COMMIT_MODEL` names keep working as fallbacks after the rename, or is a hard rename fine? A: Fallback + warning — honor the old names when the new ones are unset, with a one-line stderr deprecation warning.
- [x] Q: Where should the shared AI helpers live, and how should the `commit backend X` / `commit status` subcommands relate to `qq`? A: New `lib/ai.sh` holding renamed `_dotfiles_ai_*` helpers + `qq`; `commit backend X` exports `DOTFILES_AI_BACKEND` (switches qq too); `commit status` also shows the qq timeout; `qq` has no subcommands.
- [x] Q: With no args, how should `qq` read the question (plain `read -e` line vs. multi-line vs. `$EDITOR`)? A: Single line via `read -e -r` at a `qq> ` prompt; empty input / Ctrl-D / Ctrl-C exits without calling the AI.
- [x] Q: With args (`qq this is a question`), how should special characters be handled — accept as-is, or detect likely-mangled input and error? A: Option 3 — read the raw typed line from history via `alias qq='_dotfiles_qq #'` + `history 1`, with a leading-space guard that errors instead of sending a stale entry. (Rejected: plain `"$*"` like `c` — silent redirects/expansion; `"$*"` + noglob alias — only fixes `?`/`*`. Detecting special chars and erroring is not feasible because bash mangles args before the function runs.)
- [x] Q: What should `qq` send to the backend besides the question — raw question only, or a short wrapper instruction (e.g. "answer concisely for a terminal")? A: Short fixed terminal wrapper prepended to the question (no env override).
- [x] Q: Should `qq` give the backend access to the current directory/repo (tools, file reads), or run context-free? A: Context-free — no repo/file access; run outside the cwd and disable tools where supported.
- [x] Q: What default should `DOTFILES_QQ_TIMEOUT` have? A: 60s (parser mirrors commit's: empty/non-numeric → default, `0` → no timeout).
- [x] Q: Approve the presented design section 1 (output, spinner, errors/exit codes)? A: Yes — approved as presented.
- [x] Q: Approve the presented design section 2 (refactor scope + testing)? A: Yes — approved as presented.

</details>
title: feat(shell): add qq one-off AI question command
